prompt:
A model rocket of total mass 650 g is fired vertically upwards. The rocket motor generates a steady upward thrust of 12.5 N. An opposing atmospheric drag force of 1.8 N acts on the rocket during the ascent. Take g = 9.81 m s^-2.
(a) Calculate the weight of the rocket. [1]
(b) Determine the magnitude and direction of the resultant force acting on the rocket. [2]
(c) Calculate the upward acceleration of the rocket. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Converts mass to 0.650 kg and calculates weight W = mg = 0.650 * 9.81 = 6.38 N (accept 6.4 N).
Calculates resultant force = 12.5 - 8.18 = 4.32 N (or 4.3 N) directed upwards.
Calculates acceleration a = 4.32 / 0.650 = 6.65 m s^-2 (accept 6.6 or 6.7 m s^-2).

hints: Convert mass from grams to kilograms before calculating weight.
Weight and drag both point downwards against the upward thrust.
Divide the resultant upward force by mass in kg to obtain acceleration.
solution:
(a) m = 0.650 kg. W = 0.650 * 9.81 = 6.38 N.
(b) Total downward force = 6.38 + 1.8 = 8.18 N. Resultant force = 12.5 - 8.18 = 4.32 N upwards (or 4.3 N upwards).
(c) a = F / m = 4.32 / 0.650 = 6.65 m s^-2 upwards.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (b): Downward forces are weight (6.38 N) and drag (1.8 N), total 8.18 N. Net force is 12.5 - 8.18 = 4.32 N upward.
